verified_claims: Lopez & Bliss (2024), 'Bye-bye, bye advantage', Frontiers in Behavioral Economics / arXiv:2408.10867: 5,679 regular-season games 2002-2023. HFA was +2.69 (2002) and +1.65 (2023); market-implied HFA in 2023 was +1.74. The bye/Thursday/Monday table matches the paper exactly: bye pre-2011 margin +2.21 (0.61-3.80) vs spread +0.39 (0.00-0.78); post-2011 margin +0.31 (-1.01 to 1.64) vs spread +0.97 (0.65-1.28); Thursday +0.48 (-0.65 to 1.57) vs -0.06; off Monday night +0.14 (-0.86 to 1.18) vs +0.37 (0.14-0.61). The paper gives a 96.6% probability that the bye advantage declined after 2011.

Higgs & Stavness (2021), Scientific Reports 11:14521, seasons 2016-2020: pooled pre-COVID NFL home-advantage parameter mean 0.078. NFL HFA was already falling, 2019 was lower than 2020, and COVID restrictions did not move it off its trend.

Kelly & Chen, Research in Business and Economics Journal vol. 14 (read in full): betting the under on totals of 47.5+ went 59.7% in 2001-2009 and lost (47.1%) in 2010-2018. A threshold of median + 7 also lost (48.5%). The authors attribute this to changed sportsbook pricing behavior.

Borghesi (2008), Applied Financial Economics 18(12):947-953, data 1984-2004: heat, wind and rain lower scoring and totals prices underreact. The abstract says the strategy uses FORECASTED weather and wins significantly above 52.38% out of sample.

Nichols (2014), J. Sports Econ. 15(1):78-96, 1981-2004: visitors travelling west to east across a time zone raise home win probability; bettors underestimate the home score; no profitable strategy out of sample.

Murray (2018), J. Sports Econ., doi 10.1177/1527002516672059, 2011-2015: rest combinations affect home win probability and total points, moderated by familiarity and travel (abstract level only, as the report says).
Smith et al. (2013), SLEEP, per the AASM summary: 1970-2011, 106 night games (after 8pm ET), 293 day-game controls, West Coast teams beat the spread 66% of the time by 5.26 points on average.
nflreadr dictionary: temp and wind are 'at the stadium' (observed, not forecast); gametime is Eastern time; home_rest, away_rest, div_game and roof exist. Using game-day wind is lookahead.

greerreNFL/nfelohfa exists and has no license (GitHub license null). It is actively maintained (last push 2026-09-12). Method as described: rolling regression of past HFA with EMA smoothing, plus bye/timezone/surface/matchup-type adjustments.
The nfelo HFA tracker says divisional HFA is 'much smaller' with no numbers, and that recent league HFA is closer to 1.5 than 2.5.
Lopez, Matthews & Baumer (arXiv:1701.05976; AoAS 2018) use Bayesian state-space models on betting market data, so any HFA they estimate is market-derived.

Re-running situational_resid.py read-only reproduces every local number in the report: 6,555 games; era HFA figures; bye, Thursday, time-zone, primetime, divisional and Denver coefficients; wind buckets (-0.96/-1.62/-1.93 with n=339/187/110); pooled wind slope -0.17 (se 0.05); walk-forward totals RMSE 13.158 -> 13.133 with wind; margin walk-forward 12.906 -> 12.930-12.945; 2022 wind present in 107 of 284 rows; westnight n=30 at -5.08 (se 2.32).
The existing code in nfl-ensemble.js does contain FLAT_WEATHER_POINTS = { dome: 1.2, wind: -2.4, cold: -1.6 } used by weather_total.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: The local check does not replicate Smith et al.: Pacific visitors at Eastern home teams at night came in at -5.08, 'the opposite sign'.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: REFUTED, the sign was misread. The regression target is home margin minus the line, so -5.08 means the West Coast visitor beat the line by about 5 points. That matches Smith's +5.26 in both direction and size, and the sign is negative in every era (-6.06, -5.22, -2.38). n=30 and the pooled t is -2.2, so it is still weak evidence. But it replicates the direction, it does not contradict it.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Wind on totals is 'the only factor with consistent sign across eras' / 'Only the wind slope survives consistency across eras'.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: False on the report's own output. Several other coefficients keep one sign in all three eras: primetime totals (-0.24, -0.53, -1.93), divisional totals (-0.73, -1.50, -0.15), missing-wind totals (-0.81, -2.40, -2.67), and the westnight margin effect. Wind has the strongest pooled t (-3.2), but it is not the only consistent-sign factor.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Press coverage of Lopez, Matthews & Baumer (MSU Denver) reports Denver with the largest home advantage in the NFL.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Unsupported. The MSU Denver article gives only the Nuggets' NBA edge (about 67% vs an equal team) and says nothing about Denver's NFL home advantage. The NFL claim was not found in the cited source.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: 'About 40 coefficients tested, so about 2 with |t|>2 expected by chance.'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Understated. The script estimates 10 margin and 10 totals slope coefficients (plus intercepts) in each of 4 fits (3 eras + pooled), about 80 non-intercept tests, so about 4 are expected at |t|>2. About 7 non-intercept coefficients exceed |t|=2, consistent with near-chance levels apart from the pooled wind slope.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: nflverse spread_line/total_line is not confirmed to be the closing line; the totals intercept may be a line-source artifact.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Partly resolved by a read-only DB check. For 2020+, nflverse total_line equals nfl_nfelo_games.total_line_close in 91% of 1,621 matched games (mean absolute difference 0.06), and the spread matches the close in 69%. Against the nfelo close total, 2020+ outdoor games give an intercept of about +1.83 and a wind slope of -0.19 (iid se 0.08, n=947). So the wind leftover and the positive intercept are NOT artifacts of the line source for 2020+. Before 2020 it remains unverified.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Forecast wind exists 2022+, about 800 outdoor games.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Roughly right, with a provenance caveat. nfl_game_weather_forecast_history has about 186-193 games per season for 2022-2025 (about 750 total, matching outdoor counts), lead_days 0-5, source 'open-meteo-previous-runs'. It was all backfilled on 2026-09-02, so fetched_at is NOT a vintage timestamp. Point-in-time has to be enforced from kickoff minus lead_days. This is gridded NWP output, not the forecast the book saw.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Descriptive blog numbers (nflanalytic HFA +2.7 vs +1.7; FanDuel Thursday cover 55.7% and unders flipping).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Not checked. They are low-weight, uncontrolled blog figures and should drive no design decision.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Higgs & Stavness beta 0.078 = 'about a 7.8% multiplicative boost to points'.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Approximately right. On a log-link scale exp(0.078) is about 8.1%. This is minor.

recommendations_to_drop_or_change: Rec B4 (grade the bye-overvaluation and forecast-wind-under hypotheses on closing-line value): this is logically wrong for these two hypotheses. Both claim the CLOSING price itself is biased (Lopez & Bliss measure the spread; Borghesi and the local check measure totals vs the line). A bet that exploits a bias in the close shows no CLV even when it is +EV. Grade them on outcome residual vs the close (ATS/O-U vs closing number, with a pre-registered sample size). Use CLV only for timing and execution edge.

Rec B4 'only two situational hypotheses': given the corrected sign, the West Coast night-game effect replicates Smith's direction in every era and belongs in the registry as a third, low-prior hypothesis. If it stays out, say that was a choice, not a finding of noise.

Rec B1 and C1 (keep a situational feature only if it lowers walk-forward RMSE; port situational_resid.py as a per-feature acceptance test): this rebuilds the binary evidence gate the brief wants removed. Selecting about 10 features on the same walk-forward RMSE makes that out-of-sample number in-sample. Keep all situational features in the model with fixed, pre-declared ridge/hierarchical priors, and evaluate the whole model once walk-forward. Do not include or exclude features one at a time.

Rec B1 'bye prior about +0.3': this is the post-2011 Lopez & Bliss estimate from data through 2023. Using it as a prior in a 2011-2025 walk-forward backtest leaks test-period information. In backtests, priors must come only from data before each fold, or be neutral (0).

Rec C1 (port situational_resid.py): the script trains and evaluates on game-day wind (lookahead), and codes outdoor games with missing wind as wind=0 (calm), mixing missing with calm. It is fine as a diagnostic. It must not be ported as a production harness without swapping in forecast wind at the bet's lead time and handling missing values explicitly.

Rec B3 (fit one continuous wind slope walk-forward): do not transfer the game-day-wind slope (-0.17 to -0.24) to forecast wind. Fit the forecast-wind slope directly on the approximately 750 outdoor games from 2022-2025 with strong shrinkage toward 0, and expect it to be smaller. About 4 seasons cannot confirm it; treat its size as unknown.

Rec B2 'HFA currently about 1.5-1.8': don't treat this as a constant. The nfelo tracker currently shows 2.24 over the last 16 weeks, which shows how noisy short-window HFA is. Let the state-space or EMA estimate carry it, with no hard-coded range.
Rec C (Lopez Matthews Baumer / Denver priced by construction): drop the Denver NFL claim. It is unsourced. The local Denver residual (pooled +0.13, se 0.90) is enough on its own.
corrected_summary: What holds up after checking. (1) HFA fell from about 2.7 points in the early 2000s to about 1.65 in 2023, and the market followed: its implied HFA in 2023 was 1.74 (Lopez & Bliss 2024, arXiv:2408.10867). The decline started before COVID (Higgs & Stavness 2021, Sci Rep 11:14521). In the local check the residual home edge beyond the line is not significant in any era, so HFA should be a dynamic, shrunk state with no fixed 2.5-3 value. nfelohfa (unlicensed, active) is a pattern to copy in spirit only. (2) Bye weeks: after 2011 the true effect is +0.31 (CrI -1.01 to 1.64) and the spread prices +0.97 (0.65-1.28). Thursday and Monday effects on margin are not significant. With about 32 bye team-games a season, the roughly 0.66-point gap cannot be confirmed from this app's data. (3) Travel and time zones: Nichols (2014) found a bias but no out-of-sample profit. The local time-zone and distance effects flip sign or are not significant. Denver is not significant locally; the report's claim of the largest NFL HFA for Denver is unsourced. (4) The report misread the circadian effect. West Coast visitors in Eastern night games beat the line by about 5 points locally (n=30, t=-2.2, same sign in all eras). That replicates Smith et al. (2013) in direction, but it is too small a sample to act on. (5) Totals and wind: the pooled slope is -0.17 points/mph (se 0.05), the strongest leftover in the data. It is consistent with Borghesi (2008), whose out-of-sample strategy used forecast weather. It survives against nfelo closing totals for 2020+ (-0.19, se about 0.08), and nflverse lines match the nfelo close about 91% of the time for totals from 2020 on. But it is measured on game-day wind (lookahead), so it is an upper bound. The walk-forward gain is small (RMSE 13.158 -> 13.133). Primetime totals, divisional totals and missing-wind totals also keep a negative sign across eras but are weak, so wind is not uniquely consistent. Documented inefficiencies decay (Kelly & Chen: 59.7% unders in 2001-09, gone in 2010-18). (6) Adding every situational feature to the line made walk-forward margin RMSE worse (12.906 -> 12.93-12.95) even with a strong ridge penalty, so spreads have no exploitable situational edge. Corrected recommendations: keep situational features inside the forecast model under fixed, pre-declared shrinkage priors (no per-feature keep/drop gates, and no priors estimated from test-period data). Replace the flat weather constants (dome +1.2, wind -2.4, cold -1.6 in nfl-ensemble.js) with a continuous forecast-wind slope, fitted on nfl_game_weather_forecast_history (open-meteo previous-runs, about 750 outdoor games 2022-2025, backfilled, so point-in-time comes from kickoff minus lead_days) and shrunk hard toward zero. Fix missing-wind coverage (2022: 91 outdoor games missing). Pre-register the bye, forecast-wind and West-Coast-night hypotheses and grade them on results against the closing number, not on CLV, because the claimed bias sits in the close itself.
